SRC-153:R001.text: A first-class durable versus ephemeral contract defines sole-copy safety and explicit ownership, lifetime and recovery.

SRC-153:R002.text: Machine policy supports arbitrary user-defined ephemeral roots and explicit durable roots through the existing user configuration mechanism.

SRC-153:R003.text: Known OS or custom ephemeral roots reject durable state before canonical publication; Windows case, slashes, relative paths and links cannot bypass classification; unknown paths do not gain trust.

SRC-153:R004.text: RUN and SESSION scratch remain usable and disposable, including unavailable optional scratch; PROJECT, PERMANENT and REBOOT storage requires DURABLE.

SRC-153:R005.text: Canonical artifacts require allowed durable copies; registry referential integrity and existence are checked at validation and Work completion boundaries.

SRC-153:R006.text: Projects declare named stores with class, path, lifetime, owner and recovery; declaration and registry authority are durable when holding durable stores.

SRC-153:R007.text: Missing canonical state is explicitly detected, retained in the registry and classified RECONSTRUCTABLE, PARTIAL or UNRECOVERABLE with exact artifact paths and deterministic rebuild provenance where applicable.

SRC-153:R008.text: Promotion and bounded legacy migration copy and hash-verify files or directory trees before atomic reference publication; source files, unrelated user data and old pointers survive failure.

SRC-153:R009.text: Regression controls cover ephemeral SAILEARN adapters/cards/manifests, transient checkpoint promotion, scratch disappearance, interrupted publication and concurrent policy changes.
